key_insight: DreamTrue makes robot world models follow actions more faithfully by turning action trajectories into image-space guidance and correcting calibration issues offline. It also learns from counterfactual post-training so predictions remain physically plausible even for failed or unusual interactions.
problem_solved: Existing robot video prediction models often struggle with inaccurate action following due to poor calibration across embodiments, and they tend to over-predict successful outcomes because training data contains too few failed interactions.
method: Render action trajectories into image-space conditions so the model can better align predicted motion with commanded actions across different robot embodiments.
Apply offline geometric calibration to reduce calibration errors and improve action-faithful prediction.
Use counterfactual post-training to expose the model to alternative, failure-like outcomes, improving robustness and physical realism.
Train a multi-view, cross-embodiment robot world model for video prediction that is both action-faithful and physically plausible.
impact: This work can improve robot planning, simulation, and policy learning by making predicted future scenes more trustworthy. For practitioners, it means better model-based robotics systems that generalize across robots and handle failures more realistically.

paper_title: DreamTrue: Action-Faithful Robot World Model with Counterfactual Post-Training
paper_authors: Junyan Li, Ruizhi Li, Yu Liu, Xiangshuo Liu, Mingchao Sun
